stem: A retail study measures customer satisfaction score across 4 chains, each containing multiple stores. chain A has 8 observations with mean 43.2 /10 (within-chain SD = 6.3). chain B has 20 observations with mean 61.9 /10 (within-chain SD = 7.1). chain C has 8 observations with mean 47.5 /10 (within-chain SD = 6.3). chain D has 10 observations with mean 37.9 /10 (within-chain SD = 8.4). The between-chain standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 4.4 and 11.1 /10. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true customer satisfaction score for chain D, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-chain variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for chain D: 39.4 /10 (shrunk from raw 37.9). Range [38.6, 41.4] as between-chain SD varies from 4.4 to 11.1. Pooled mean: 50.9.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 50.9 /10 (weighted average of 4 chain means).
Shrinkage factor for chain D: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/10). At σ_between=7.4: B = 0.886.
Interval [38.6, 41.4] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (37.9) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (50.9) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
